Home advantage is significant—Arsenal have won 5 of 6 home CL games this season and conceded only 11 PL goals at the Emirates. Atletico rotated 11 players to win 2-0 at Valencia and arrive fresh, but they have lost 3 of 6 away CL games and traveled poorly this season. Key absences: Merino (out), Timber (out); Odegaard and Havertz are racing to return, Saka was managed at HT vs Fulham. Atletico miss Pablo Barrios and Nico Gonzalez; Hancko/G. Simeone doubts. Tactically Simeone will sit deep and counter through Alvarez, Griezmann and Lookman (Atleti xG 2.22 in leg 1), while Arsenal will dominate possession and need to break a low block, with Eze, Saka and Gyokeres providing the cutting edge. Tie level + must-win incentive + open box means realistic mass on 2-1, 1-1, 2-2, but Arsenal favored. Opta supercomputer puts Arsenal at 56% to win in normal time.

reasoning.t3_events: Expect Arsenal to press early at the Emirates with a charged crowd; Atleti will absorb and look for set pieces and Alvarez/Lookman transitions. Tactical fouling from Atleti likely produces multiple yellow cards; goals tilted to second half as Atleti tire. Knockout context means extra time is plausible if level at 90'.
